documents.text: Business Model Canvas (BMC): The Business Model Canvas (BMC) is a strategic management tool that provides a visual framework for developing, describing, and analyzing business models. The expanded SDG-adapted version consists of 11 interconnected building blocks, including Social and Environmental Cost and Social and Environmental Benefit.

BMC - Customer Segments: Defines the different groups of people or organizations an enterprise aims to reach and serve. Customers comprise the heart of any business model. Key questions: For whom are we creating value? Who are our most important customers? What are the customer archetypes? Examples: Mass market, Niche market, Segmented, Diversified, Multi-sided platforms.

BMC - Value Propositions: Describes the bundle of products and services that create value for a specific Customer Segment. It solves a customer problem or satisfies a need. Key questions: What value do we deliver to the customer? Which customer needs are we satisfying? What bundles of products/services are we offering? Examples: Newness, Performance, Customization, Getting the job done, Design, Brand/Status, Price, Cost reduction, Risk reduction, Accessibility, Convenience.

BMC - Channels: Describes how a company communicates with and reaches its Customer Segments to deliver a Value Proposition. Channels serve several functions: awareness, evaluation, purchase, delivery, and after-sales. Key questions: Through which channels do our customers want to be reached? How do we reach them now? Which channels work best and are most cost-efficient? Examples: Direct: Sales force, Web sales, Own stores, Indirect: Partner stores, Wholesaler.

BMC - Customer Relationships: Describes the types of relationships a company establishes with specific Customer Segments. Motivations: customer acquisition, customer retention, boosting sales. Key questions: What type of relationship does each segment expect? Which ones have we established? How costly are they? Examples: Personal assistance, Dedicated personal assistance, Self-service, Automated services, Communities, Co-creation.

BMC - Revenue Streams: Represents the cash a company generates from each Customer Segment. Revenue Streams can involve one-time transactions or recurring revenues. Key questions: For what value are customers willing to pay? What are they currently paying for? How would they prefer to pay? Examples: Asset sale, Usage fee, Subscription, Lending/Renting/Leasing, Licensing, Brokerage fees, Advertising.

BMC - Key Resources: Describes the most important assets required to make a business model work. They allow an enterprise to create and offer value, reach markets, and earn revenues. Key questions: What key resources do our value propositions require? Our distribution channels? Customer relationships? Examples: Physical (facilities, equipment), Intellectual (brands, patents, data), Human (key employees), Financial (cash, credit lines).

BMC - Key Activities: Describes the most important things a company must do to make its business model work. These are the critical actions for creating Value Propositions. Key questions: What key activities do our value propositions require? Our distribution channels? Revenue streams? Examples: Production, Problem solving, Platform/Network management, Supply chain management, Marketing.

BMC - Key Partnerships: Describes the network of suppliers and partners that make the business model work. Companies forge partnerships to optimize, reduce risk, or acquire resources. Key questions: Who are our key partners and suppliers? Which key resources are we acquiring from partners? Which key activities do partners perform? Examples: Strategic alliances, Coopetition, Joint ventures, Buyer-supplier relationships.

BMC - Cost Structure: Describes all costs incurred to operate a business model. Costs can be cost-driven (minimize costs) or value-driven (premium value creation). Key questions: What are the most important costs inherent in our business model? Which key resources are most expensive? Which key activities are most expensive? Examples: Fixed costs, Variable costs, Economies of scale, Economies of scope.

BMC - Social and Environmental Cost: Describes the negative social and environmental impacts (externalities) of the business model — emissions, waste, resource depletion, community harm, or health risks. Key questions: What negative social impacts does our business model create? What environmental harm or resource depletion results from our operations? Who bears these costs and can they be mitigated? Examples: Carbon emissions, Plastic waste, Water pollution, Community displacement, Health risks from production.

BMC - Social and Environmental Benefit: Describes the positive social and environmental contributions of the business model — jobs created, access to essential services, carbon reduction, education, or health improvements. Often mapped to UN SDGs. Key questions: What positive outcomes does our business create for society? What environmental improvements result from our model? Which SDGs does our business advance? Examples: Clean water access, Job creation in underserved communities, Carbon reduction, Reduced disease burden, SDG alignment.

SWOT strengths: Internal positive attributes and resources that support achieving objectives. Questions: What do we do well? What unique resources do we have? What do others see as our strengths? What competitive advantages do we have?

SWOT weaknesses: Internal factors that detract from the ability to achieve objectives. Questions: What could we improve? Where do we have fewer resources than others? What are others likely to see as weaknesses? What factors lose us sales?

SWOT opportunities: External factors the organization could exploit to its advantage. Questions: What trends could we take advantage of? What opportunities are open to us? What technology changes could benefit us? What policy/regulatory changes may benefit us?

SWOT threats: External factors that could cause trouble for the organization. Questions: What obstacles do we face? What are our competitors doing? Are quality standards or specifications changing? Is changing technology threatening our position?

Porter's Five Forces - Threat of New Entrants: How easy or difficult it is for new competitors to enter the industry. Factors: Barriers to entry, Capital requirements, Brand loyalty, Economies of scale, Government regulations.
Porter's Five Forces - Bargaining Power of Suppliers: How much pressure suppliers can place on a business. Factors: Number of suppliers, Uniqueness of supply, Switching costs, Supplier concentration.

Porter's Five Forces - Bargaining Power of Buyers: How much pressure customers can place on a business. Factors: Number of customers, Size of orders, Price sensitivity, Buyer information availability.

Porter's Five Forces - Threat of Substitutes: How easily customers can find alternative products or services. Factors: Number of substitutes available, Buyer propensity to substitute, Relative price performance, Switching costs.

Porter's Five Forces - Industry Rivalry: The intensity of competition among existing competitors. Factors: Number of competitors, Industry growth rate, Product differentiation, Exit barriers, Fixed cost levels.

Value Proposition Canvas: The Value Proposition Canvas helps ensure that a product or service is positioned around what the customer values and needs.. Customer Profile: Jobs (Tasks customers are trying to perform, problems they're trying to solve, or needs they want to satisfy), Pains (Negative outcomes, risks, and obstacles related to customer jobs), Gains (Outcomes and benefits customers want).
Business Model - Freemium: Basic service is free; premium features require payment. Best for: Digital products with low marginal costs and network effects. Examples: Spotify, Dropbox, LinkedIn.

Business Model - Subscription: Recurring revenue through periodic payments for continued access. Best for: Services with ongoing value delivery and predictable costs. Examples: Netflix, SaaS products, Gym memberships.
Business Model - Marketplace/Platform: Connect buyers and sellers, taking a fee for facilitating transactions. Best for: Industries with fragmented supply and demand. Examples: Airbnb, Uber, Etsy.

Business Model - Razor and Blades: Sell the base product cheaply, profit from consumables/add-ons. Best for: Products requiring regular replenishment. Examples: Printers/ink, Gaming consoles/games, Coffee machines/pods.

Business Model - Direct-to-Consumer (D2C): Sell directly to end consumers, bypassing traditional retail. Best for: Brands wanting control over customer experience and data. Examples: Warby Parker, Dollar Shave Club, Casper.

Business Model - Pay-as-you-go: Customers pay based on actual usage rather than a fixed fee. Best for: Variable-demand services where usage varies significantly. Examples: AWS, Utility companies, Pay-per-use insurance.

Business Model - Social Enterprise: Business model that prioritizes social/environmental impact alongside financial sustainability. Best for: Organizations balancing profit with purpose. Examples: TOMS Shoes, Grameen Bank, Patagonia.

Dilemma Triangle - People: Social equity, fair labor practices, community development, human rights, stakeholder well-being. Tensions: Short-term profits vs. fair wages; Growth vs. community impact; Efficiency vs. worker well-being.

Dilemma Triangle - Planet: Environmental sustainability, resource conservation, emissions reduction, biodiversity, circular economy. Tensions: Cost reduction vs. environmental compliance; Growth vs. resource limits; Convenience vs. sustainability.

Dilemma Triangle - Prosperity: Economic viability, profitability, long-term growth, financial inclusion, shared value creation. Tensions: Short-term returns vs. long-term sustainability; Shareholder value vs. stakeholder value; Scale vs. localization.

SDG 1 - No Poverty: End poverty in all its forms everywhere. Poverty encompasses lack of income and productive resources to ensure sustainable livelihoods.. Targets: Eradicate extreme poverty (less than $2.15/day); Reduce at least by half the proportion of people living in poverty; Implement social protection systems and measures for all. Business applications: Fair wage policies and living wage commitments; Financial inclusion products (microfinance, mobile banking); Supply chain practices that uplift smallholders; Affordable products and services for base-of-pyramid markets.

SDG 2 - Zero Hunger: End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition, and promote sustainable agriculture.. Targets: End hunger and ensure access to safe and nutritious food; End all forms of malnutrition; Double agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers. Business applications: Sustainable agriculture and food production; Food waste reduction initiatives; Nutrition-focused product development; Supporting smallholder farmers in supply chains.

SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-being: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages.. Targets: Reduce maternal mortality and end preventable deaths of newborns; End epidemics and combat diseases; Achieve universal health coverage. Business applications: Affordable healthcare products and services; Workplace health and safety programs; Mental health and well-being initiatives; Health-tech innovations for underserved populations.

SDG 4 - Quality Education: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.. Targets: Ensure all children complete quality primary and secondary education; Equal access to affordable technical and higher education; Substantially increase the number of youth and adults with relevant skills. Business applications: Employee training and development programs; EdTech products and services; Apprenticeship and internship programs; Educational partnerships with communities.

SDG 5 - Gender Equality: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls.. Targets: End all forms of discrimination against women and girls; Ensure women's full and effective participation in leadership; Ensure universal access to reproductive health and rights. Business applications: Gender-balanced hiring and leadership development; Equal pay audits and policies; Products and services addressing women's needs; Women-owned supplier programs.

SDG 6 - Clean Water and Sanitation: Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.. Targets: Achieve universal and equitable access to safe drinking water; Achieve access to adequate sanitation and hygiene; Improve water quality by reducing pollution. Business applications: Water efficiency in operations; Water purification products and services; Wastewater treatment and recycling; Community water access programs.

SDG 7 - Affordable and Clean Energy: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all.. Targets: Ensure universal access to affordable and reliable energy; Increase the share of renewable energy; Double the global rate of improvement in energy efficiency. Business applications: Renewable energy adoption and generation; Energy-efficient products and operations; Off-grid energy solutions for underserved areas; Clean energy technology development.

SDG 8 - Decent Work and Economic Growth: Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.. Targets: Sustain per capita economic growth; Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through innovation; Promote development-oriented policies for productive activities and decent job creation. Business applications: Fair labor practices and living wages; Job creation in underserved communities; Supply chain labor standards; Innovation and productivity improvements.

SDG 9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation.. Targets: Develop quality, reliable and resilient infrastructure; Promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization; Enhance scientific research and upgrade industrial technologies. Business applications: Sustainable infrastructure development; R&D investment in clean technologies; Digital infrastructure for underserved areas; Industrial process optimization.

SDG 10 - Reduced Inequalities: Reduce inequality within and among countries.. Targets: Progressively achieve income growth of the bottom 40%; Empower and promote social, economic and political inclusion; Ensure equal opportunity and reduce inequalities of outcome. Business applications: Inclusive hiring practices; Products accessible to marginalized communities; Progressive wage structures; Diversity, equity, and inclusion programs.

SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable.. Targets: Ensure access to adequate, safe and affordable housing; Provide access to sustainable transport systems; Reduce the adverse environmental impact of cities. Business applications: Sustainable urban development projects; Green building and construction; Sustainable mobility solutions; Community-centered design and planning.

SDG 12 - Responsible Consumption and Production: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.. Targets: Implement the 10-year framework on sustainable consumption and production; Achieve sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources; Halve per capita global food waste at retail and consumer levels. Business applications: Circular economy business models; Sustainable packaging and materials; Product lifecycle management; Waste reduction and recycling programs.

SDG 13 - Climate Action: Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.. Targets: Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards; Integrate climate change measures into policies and planning; Improve education and awareness on climate change. Business applications: Carbon footprint reduction and net-zero targets; Climate risk assessment and adaptation; Carbon offset and removal projects; Climate-resilient supply chains.

SDG 14 - Life Below Water: Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development.. Targets: Prevent and reduce marine pollution; Sustainably manage and protect marine ecosystems; End overfishing and destructive fishing practices. Business applications: Plastic pollution reduction; Sustainable seafood sourcing; Marine-friendly product design; Ocean conservation partnerships.

SDG 15 - Life on Land: Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, manage forests sustainably, combat desertification, and halt biodiversity loss.. Targets: Ensure conservation of terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems; Promote sustainable forest management; Combat desertification and restore degraded land. Business applications: Sustainable land use and forestry; Biodiversity-positive supply chains; Deforestation-free commitments; Habitat restoration projects.

SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: Promote peaceful and inclusive societies, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable institutions.. Targets: Significantly reduce all forms of violence; Promote the rule of law and ensure equal access to justice; Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions. Business applications: Anti-corruption policies and transparency; Ethical governance and compliance; Human rights due diligence; Stakeholder engagement and accountability.

SDG 17 - Partnerships for the Goals: Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development.. Targets: Enhance global macroeconomic stability; Enhance policy coherence for sustainable development; Enhance the global partnership for sustainable development. Business applications: Cross-sector collaboration and partnerships; Knowledge sharing and capacity building; Multi-stakeholder initiatives; Technology transfer and open innovation.

Market Sizing - TAM (Total Addressable Market): The total market demand for a product or service, assuming 100% market share with no competition. Represents the maximum revenue opportunity.. Methods: Top-down: Start with industry reports, narrow by geography and segment; Bottom-up: Number of potential customers × average revenue per customer; Value theory: How much value does your solution create for the market?.

Market Sizing - SAM (Serviceable Addressable Market): The segment of TAM targeted by your products/services that is within your geographic reach and fits your business model.. Methods: TAM filtered by: geography, customer type, pricing tier, distribution capability; Focus on segments you can actually reach with your current business model.

Market Sizing - SOM (Serviceable Obtainable Market): The portion of SAM that you can realistically capture in the near term (1-3 years), considering competition and resources.. Methods: SAM × realistic market share (typically 1-5% for startups in year 1); Bottom-up from sales capacity, marketing budget, and conversion rates; Comparable company analysis: what share did similar companies achieve?.
Revenue Model - Transaction-based: Revenue from each sale or transaction. Industries: Retail, E-commerce, Marketplaces. Metrics: Average order value, Transaction frequency, Customer lifetime value.

Revenue Model - Subscription/Recurring: Predictable recurring revenue from periodic payments. Industries: SaaS, Media, Health & Wellness, Education. Metrics: MRR/ARR, Churn rate, LTV:CAC ratio, Net revenue retention.

Revenue Model - Advertising/Attention: Revenue from displaying ads to an audience. Industries: Media, Social platforms, Search engines, Free apps. Metrics: CPM, CPC, DAU/MAU, Time on platform, Ad fill rate.

Revenue Model - Licensing/IP: Revenue from allowing others to use intellectual property. Industries: Technology, Entertainment, Franchising, Patents. Metrics: License fees, Royalty rates, Number of licensees, IP portfolio value.

Revenue Model - Service/Consulting: Revenue from professional services and expertise. Industries: Consulting, Healthcare, Legal, Design, Engineering. Metrics: Billable hours, Project value, Utilization rate, Client retention.

Revenue Model - Data Monetization: Revenue from insights generated by data collection and analysis. Industries: Analytics, IoT, FinTech, HealthTech. Metrics: Data volume, Insight accuracy, Customer decisions influenced.

Revenue Model - Impact/Outcome-based: Revenue tied to measurable outcomes or social/environmental impact. Industries: Social enterprises, Impact investing, Pay-for-success programs. Metrics: Social ROI, Impact metrics achieved, Cost savings generated.

Customer Segment - Early Adopters: Tech-savvy, risk-tolerant customers who try new products first. Characteristics: High tolerance for imperfection; Value innovation over polish; Influence others; Willing to pay premium for novelty. Reach: Product communities, tech blogs, beta programs, influencer partnerships.

Customer Segment - Price-Sensitive Pragmatists: Value-focused customers who prioritize cost-effectiveness. Characteristics: Comparison shoppers; Wait for reviews; Prefer proven solutions; Sensitive to switching costs. Reach: Price comparison sites, referral programs, free trials, money-back guarantees.

Customer Segment - Conscious Consumers: Customers who factor social and environmental impact into purchasing decisions. Characteristics: Research brand values; Willing to pay 10-25% premium for sustainability; Share values on social media; High brand loyalty when values align. Reach: Sustainability certifications, impact reports, purpose-driven content, community engagement.

Customer Segment - Enterprise/B2B Buyers: Organizational buyers with formal procurement processes. Characteristics: Multi-stakeholder decision-making; Long sales cycles; Require ROI justification; Value relationships and support. Reach: Account-based marketing, case studies, demos, procurement compliance, ESG reporting.

Customer Segment - Underserved/BOP Markets: Base-of-pyramid markets with significant unmet needs. Characteristics: Price-constrained; Limited access to traditional channels; Mobile-first; Community-influenced. Reach: Mobile distribution, agent networks, microfinance partnerships, community trust-building.

Channel - Omnichannel Integration: Seamless customer experience across all touchpoints (online, offline, mobile). Considerations: Channel consistency; Data sharing across touchpoints; Customer journey mapping; Attribution modeling.

Channel - Partnership Distribution: Leveraging partner networks to reach customers at scale. Considerations: Partner alignment on values; Revenue sharing models; Brand control; Customer relationship ownership.

Channel - Community-Led Growth: Building communities around your product that drive organic growth. Considerations: Community management resources; Authenticity; Value exchange with community members.

Channel - Digital-First Distribution: Prioritizing digital channels for discovery, acquisition, and delivery. Considerations: Customer acquisition cost; Channel saturation; Content quality requirements; Technical infrastructure.

Financial Planning - Unit Economics: Revenue and costs associated with a single unit of your business model. Metrics: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Lifetime Value (LTV), LTV:CAC ratio (target: >3:1), Payback period, Gross margin per unit.
Financial Planning - Break-even Analysis: The point at which total revenue equals total costs.
Financial Planning - Financial Projections: 3-5 year forward-looking financial estimates.

Business Plan Section 1. Executive Summary: Provide a concise overview of the business, value proposition, target market, and strategic direction. Key questions: What problem does the business solve? Who is the primary customer? What is the unique value proposition? What are the top 3 strategic priorities? Example metrics: Target market size, Revenue model summary, Key SDG alignment. Anti-hallucination rules: Do not invent revenue figures not supported by BMC or SWOT Reference the selected value proposition by name Only claim SDG alignment supported by prior mapping

Business Plan Section 2. Market Opportunity: Describe the market need, size, trends, and why now is the right time. Key questions: Who experiences the problem most acutely? What market trends support this opportunity? What is the competitive landscape? Example metrics: TAM/SAM/SOM estimates if grounded, Growth rate, Customer segment size. Anti-hallucination rules: Mark market size estimates as [INFERRED] unless sourced from user context Align customer segments with BMC customer_segments block Do not contradict SWOT opportunities or threats

Business Plan Section 3. Business Model Overview: Summarize how the business creates, delivers, and captures value using BMC blocks. Key questions: How does each BMC block contribute to the model? What are the key partnerships and resources? How does revenue flow? Example metrics: Revenue streams, Cost drivers, Key partners count. Anti-hallucination rules: Every BMC block claim must map to stored BMC content Cite block names explicitly (e.g., Key Partners, Revenue Streams) Do not add partners or channels not in the BMC

Business Plan Section 4. Product or Service Description: Explain the offering, features, and differentiation. Key questions: What is the core product or service? What pain points does it relieve? What makes it different from alternatives? Example metrics: Feature list, Delivery model, Pricing approach. Anti-hallucination rules: Ground features in value_propositions BMC block Align with selected SWOT strengths Do not invent product capabilities not implied by story or BMC

metadata.title: Business Plan - Product or Service Description

documents.text: Business Plan Section 5. Customer & Marketing Strategy: Define target customers, relationships, channels, and go-to-market approach. Key questions: Who are the primary customer segments? How will you reach and retain them? What is the customer relationship model? Example metrics: CAC assumptions [INFERRED], Channel mix, Retention strategy. Anti-hallucination rules: Use BMC customer_segments, channels, and customer_relationships blocks Match focus areas from dilemma triangle workflow Do not contradict tensions or dilemmas resolved earlier

Business Plan Section 6. Operations Plan: Describe key activities, resources, and operational delivery model. Key questions: What are the critical activities? What resources are required? How is quality and delivery ensured? Example metrics: Key activities list, Resource requirements, Operational milestones. Anti-hallucination rules: Ground in BMC key_activities and key_resources blocks Address operational risks from issues/tensions steps Do not invent facilities or headcount without marking [INFERRED]

Business Plan Section 7. Financial & Sustainability Outlook: Outline revenue model, cost structure, and financial sustainability. Key questions: What are the primary revenue streams? What are the major cost drivers? How does the model remain financially sustainable? Example metrics: Revenue streams, Cost structure, Break-even timeline [INFERRED]. Anti-hallucination rules: Use BMC revenue_streams and cost_structure blocks as source of truth Mark financial projections as [INFERRED] unless user provided numbers Align with SWOT financial opportunities and threats

Business Plan Section 8. Key Risks & Mitigation Strategies: Identify major risks and concrete mitigation approaches. Key questions: What are the top business risks? How will each risk be mitigated? What trade-offs remain unresolved? Example metrics: Risk severity, Mitigation actions, Residual risk level. Anti-hallucination rules: Draw risks from SWOT weaknesses and threats Reference ranked dilemmas and tensions from prior steps Do not dismiss risks flagged in critique agent warnings

metadata.title: Business Plan - Key Risks & Mitigation Strategies

documents.text: Business Plan Section 9. SDG Alignment & Impact: Connect the business model to UN SDGs with evidence-based claims. Key questions: Which SDGs does the business directly support? What is the evidence for each alignment? What social/environmental costs and benefits exist? Example metrics: Strong SDG alignments, Impact indicators, Social/environmental benefit items. Anti-hallucination rules: Only claim strong SDG alignment with evidence from SDG mapping or BMC impact blocks Use social_environmental_cost and social_environmental_benefit BMC blocks Avoid greenwashing — mark inferred alignments as [INFERRED]

Business Plan Section 10. Conclusion & Next Steps: Summarize strategic direction and immediate actionable next steps. Key questions: What is the strategic summary? What are the top 3 next steps? What milestones should be tracked? Example metrics: 90-day milestones, Key partnerships to pursue, Validation steps. Anti-hallucination rules: Next steps must follow logically from prior sections Do not introduce new business lines or markets not discussed earlier Reiterate selected value proposition and primary SDG focus
